title: Guild Authority
paragraphs: “Displaying their entire physique like this makes it really easy to understand.”
“It seems there’s a bounty on a group of bandits based around this area.”
“Bandits, huh?”
“They were charged with looting valuables that a certain noble was transporting and attacking an innocent village. They seem to have other crimes as well.”
“At this point, they’re not just bandits—they’re outright bounty targets.”
“Is there a difference?”
“There is indeed.”
I turned to Father and the others and began explaining. Yes, the difference between bounty targets and bandits is…
“Bandits are just resources—scattered, low-level criminals. The bounty on them is minimal, close to that of a shoplifter. By their own standards, killing is the mark of a third-rate bandit.”
“Wait, did you just call them resources!?”
“I’ve never heard anyone call bandits ‘resources’ before…”
“The one who first said that was Father in our original world. He said that since their stolen goods technically have no clear owner, they could be freely confiscated.”
“Iwatani-dono…”
“It wasn’t me! That’s a misunderstanding!”
Éclair gave Father a half-lidded stare.
“According to him, if the ownership of something is clear, that’s one thing, but he saw no reason to hand over valuables to shady people making baseless claims.”
Upon hearing this, Éclair sighed but quickly seemed to accept the reasoning.
“Indeed, it’s a constant issue—what to do with confiscated goods from bandits. It’s not like you can assume there won’t be dishonest people falsely claiming ownership.”
In fact, she added, there were plenty of such people.

“It was a problem even in Father’s territory. Proving whether a victim was truly a victim is difficult. Most of the time, the confiscated goods are used to fund the town’s vigilante groups. Otherwise, they are held until proper ownership can be verified.”
“Sounds like most cases just end with the victims having to give up.”
“It’s a grim reality. Losing something and not being able to get it back…”
“Maybe merchants need to report their valuables to nearby towns in advance?”
“Yes, but many people don’t bother. Some merchants just accept encountering bandits as bad luck and move on.”
Even if they report it to the government, the chances of getting their belongings back are slim. That’s the reality. Then, Éclair continued—
“There’s also the problem of fake victims appearing when the vigilantes conduct bandit hunts.”

She told us a story— Once, after returning stolen goods to a supposed victim, the same items were found that night at a pawnshop. The person who received them had been bragging about tricking the vigilantes into handing over valuable loot.
“That’s why cases of fake victims making claims are endless, and in many cases, the goods can’t be returned at all.”
“That’s… rotten.”
“Completely.”
“Or maybe just… resourceful?”
“So, basically, confiscating loot from bandits for yourself is hard to condemn.”

“Exactly. That’s likely why Father called them resources. I also heard rumors of groups raising their own bandits and having them hunt other bandits, redistributing the stolen loot as charity to nearby villages.”
“Is that… better? Maybe?”

Father and the others nodded, albeit with puzzled expressions. That said, hunting a small-time bandit gang wouldn’t yield much money—maybe ten gold coins at most. It would be more profitable to hunt a dragon deep in the mountains.

“Back to the main point—bounty targets are different. They are criminals with confirmed identities and undeniable proof of their crimes, with official bounties placed on them by victims and the guild.”
“So what’s the difference from bandits?”
“Capturing a bandit doesn’t pay well. Most of the time, it’s practically unpaid labor.”

In some cases, I heard, you might even have to cover their medical expenses. Even if they are clearly criminals, you never know what connections they might have behind the scenes. Huh? This is starting to bring back some memories…
“I just remembered. I heard a story—apparently, in our original world, Ren fell from grace and became the Bandit King.”
“The Bandit King…”
“Did you leave behind everything in this world or something?”
“How would I know?!”
“They say you were consumed by a cursed weapon and ended up ambushing Father.”
“Ren-san…”
Itsuki patted Ren on the shoulder with an oddly pleased expression.
What kind of reaction is that?
“As for the details… It seems you were tricked by that damned pig princess and lost everything. Or so I heard…”
I hadn’t paid much attention to the story, and by the time I arrived in the village, Ren was already there. So this is partly speculation. I’d completely forgotten about it.
“That princess again?! Does she have some kind of grudge against us?”
“Naofumi-san, Motoyasu-san, Ren-san, and then me as well.”
“What was she trying to accomplish by screwing over so many heroes…?”
Seriously. Trying to understand the actions of that filthy red pig is beyond the reasoning of normal people.
“Motoyasu, let’s get back to the topic.”
“Understood. A bounty target is, quite literally, someone you can capture for money. Depending on the conditions, taking them down outright might not be a problem.”
After all, they’re just garbage. At least they serve the purpose of making us money.
“Before Father’s false charges were cleared, Ren, Itsuki, and I all hunted them together.”
“Huh…”
“You can find sighting reports at the guild. If you capture them successfully, it’s a quick way to make a fortune.”
By the way, the payout depends on your performance.

“There were also hero-exclusive requests from the kingdom, like investigating corrupt nobles. Itsuki particularly liked those jobs. When I completed one on that damn pig princess’ request, Itsuki got all passive-aggressive about it.”
“Huh…”
Father and Ren were looking at Itsuki.
“W-what is it?”
“This has nothing to do with you now, right?”
“That’s true. We should be careful. After all, some of those so-called ‘corrupt’ lords might have actually been good rulers, just seen as bad by the country.”

“Then there are also issues faced by villages and towns. The nature of these problems varies—solving a famine, rescuing children taken by monsters, or even liberating a town controlled by a bounty target.”
Well, all of those were supposedly grand quests… but in reality, many were rather dubious.
Who knows how much deception was mixed into them?
“So it’s a kind of system for separation. Jobs below level 40 can be done by regular folks, not just adventurers, which makes competition fierce.”
“On the other hand, those who earn the country’s trust and complete their Class Up can take on high-difficulty, low-competition requests. They’re in high demand.”
“So there’s a clear distinction between adventurers, mercenaries hired by the country, and knights.”
“Ren and Itsuki, you two already knew about this, right?”
“More or less.”
“Yeah.”
“And since heroes have no level cap, we can take on even the most difficult requests.”
We all nodded. The world has its restrictions, but in a way, it’s designed pretty well.
“Oh, so it’s not some massive organization spanning across nations?”

That kind of thing is more like a religion. The Three Heroes Church and the churches of Siltvelt are exceptions, but the Four Holy Church is said to be widespread, crossing national borders. The Three Heroes Church proved how dangerous these groups can be when turned into enemies.
“But they can issue travel permits for moving between countries, right?”
“Not just the Adventurer’s Guild—many guilds have ties to their host nation, and some authority has been delegated to them,” Éclair explained.

“Iwatani-dono, what you’re saying is a bit unclear, but each city usually has two or three large Adventurer’s Guilds. Some of these guilds are backed by foreign nations. In that sense, many do extend beyond their home country, but their influence is weaker than their home base.”
“Huh… so they’re basically subcontractors.”
“Don’t call them that.”
“You’re ruining the fantasy.”
And so, we learned about the guild system.
With that, Éclair headed toward the counter.
“I’ll gather some of the information Iwatani-dono and the others are looking for. Just wait a bit.”
“Alright. We’ll take a look around on our own in the meantime.”
“Sounds good.”
“Since we’ve gotten a little stronger, let’s explore the town while we’re at it.”
And so, we decided to regroup at the guild later and went our separate ways. (A late but necessary explanation about the Adventurer’s Guild.)
